verses.pali: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, vassassa antarāyā, yaṁ nemittā na jānanti, yattha nemittānaṁ cakkhu na kamati.
verses.english: “Mendicants, there are these five obstacles to rain, which the forecasters don’t know, and which their vision does not traverse.
In the upper atmosphere the fire element flares up,

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo vassassa antarāyo, yaṁ nemittā na jānanti, yattha nemittānaṁ cakkhu na kamati.
verses.english: This is the first obstacle to rain, which the forecasters don’t know, and which their vision does not traverse.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, upari ākāse vāyodhātu pakuppati.
verses.english: Furthermore, in the upper atmosphere the air element flares up,

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo vassassa antarāyo, yaṁ nemittā na jānanti, yattha nemittānaṁ cakkhu na kamati.
verses.english: This is the second obstacle to rain …

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, rāhu asurindo pāṇinā udakaṁ sampaṭicchitvā mahāsamudde chaḍḍeti.
verses.english: Furthermore, Rāhu, lord of titans, receives water in his hand and discards it in the ocean.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo vassassa antarāyo, yaṁ nemittā na jānanti, yattha nemittānaṁ cakkhu na kamati.
verses.english: This is the third obstacle to rain …

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, vassavalāhakā devā pamattā honti.
verses.english: Furthermore, the gods of the rain clouds become negligent.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho vassassa antarāyo, yaṁ nemittā na jānanti, yattha nemittānaṁ cakkhu na kamati.
verses.english: This is the fourth obstacle to rain …

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, manussā adhammikā honti.
Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamo vassassa antarāyo, yaṁ nemittā na jānanti, yattha nemittānaṁ cakkhu na kamati.
verses.english: This is the fifth obstacle to rain, which the forecasters don’t know, and which their vision does not traverse.

verses.pali: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca vassassa antarāyā, yaṁ nemittā na jānanti, yattha nemittānaṁ cakkhu na kamatī”ti.
verses.english: These are the five obstacles to rain, which the forecasters don’t know, and which their vision does not traverse.”
